subject: Raftlytics onramp: cert rotation, split-DNS & reranker latency tradeoffs
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ryu <alex@raftlytics.com>, Helen Cho <h.cho@raftlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:23:00 +0000
Subject: Raftlytics onramp: cert rotation, split-DNS & reranker latency tradeoffs

Hi Alex / Helen — great conversation today. Quick post-call recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Networking / private connectivity
- Raftlytics will use a VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) to connect to Redwood Private control plane + inference endpoint. We recommend split-horizon DNS so internal calls resolve to the endpoint inside your VPC and public names route normally.
- IP allowlist: we can provide an output IP set for your NAT/proxy; however PrivateLink removes the need for public egress for inference traffic. If you plan additional egress (metrics, S3 uploads), we need to capture those IPs.
- mTLS: Redwood supports mutual TLS for customer-to-runtime auth. You'll generate a CSR (we can sign or accept a CA-signed cert). We discussed short-lived client certs (30d) with automated rotation — see attachments for a sample CSR and our recommended rotation playbook.

2) SDK/auth & routing
- SDKs: recommend using our JS or Python SDK with short-lived bearer tokens minted via your identity provider (OIDC) or service account keys.
- Routing policy: you can pin production traffic to a quantized CPU/GPU model variant for cost predictability and fall back to a lower-cost variant on capacity constraints.

3) Structured output & reranker
- Tool-calling / structured outputs: we support JSON schema validation on responses. For the reranker/embedding path, we usually embed top-K hits and run a lightweight model to re-rank. Tradeoff: larger K improves accuracy but increases latency and embedding cost. See the reranker-latency-note-sheet.csv attached for estimates.

Immediate next steps (proposed timeline):
- By Mon 2027-04-12: Raftlytics to confirm preferred cert flow (Redwood sign vs. customer CA) and DNS plan.
- By Tue 2027-04-13: Redwood to share PrivateLink endpoint name, IP set for optional egress, and an example Terraform snippet.
- Schedule: technical handoff call — propose Wed 2027-04-14 10:00 PT (we can shift if that doesn’t work).

If anything above is off, flag and we’ll adjust. I’ve cc'ed Ben to coordinate the mTLS cert pieces and Marissa for production-embedding/reranker sizing.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: Raftlytics onramp: cert rotation, split-DNS & reranker latency tradeoffs

Thanks Jordan — super helpful recap. A couple clarifying questions from our infra team: 

1) For split-horizon DNS, will we need to manage Route 53 records (we operate the hosted zone) or can Redwood provide a private hosted zone that we delegate?
2) For mTLS rotation, do you have an automated endpoint we can call to upload new cert material, or do we rotate directly via our proxy (Envoy) to present new client certs?
3) Embedding + reranker: can you share a sample latency profile for 256-dim vs 1536-dim embeddings when used with a 10-candidate rerank (we run tight p95 SLAs)?

Also — Helen and I are leaning towards customer-signed certs (we need to align with our Compliance team), so we’ll prepare a CA-signed cert.

Appreciate the quick follow-up.

—Alex
Alex Ryu | Head of Integrations, Raftlytics
alex@raftlytics.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ryu <alex@raftlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 11:00:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Raftlytics onramp: cert rotation, split-DNS & reranker latency tradeoffs

Alex — good questions, answers below. I’ve attached the brief CSV with measured p50/p95 numbers we see on a sample workload.

1) Split-horizon DNS: you should keep control of the hosted zone. Our recommended approach is to create a private A/CNAME record in your VPC that points at the PrivateLink endpoint DNS name that Redwood provides. We can send a Terraform snippet for Route53 private zone delegation if you want us to manage via IaC.

2) mTLS rotation: if you opt for customer-signed certs, rotation is typically handled in your proxy (Envoy/NGINX) or Secrets Manager. Redwood offers an internal endpoint for automating rotation when customers want us to store cert metadata and push rotation events to the runtime (used by some partners). For compliance, many customers rotate in their own infra and we simply accept the new certs.

3) Embedding sizes and reranker latency:
- 256-dim: lower network + compute; typical p95 for a 10-candidate rerank on a small CPU-optimized instance ~ 220-320 ms.
- 1536-dim: higher memory and dot-product cost; p95 for same rerank ~ 420-650 ms (depends on host and batching).

Notes: for strict p95 SLAs we recommend either reducing K (candidates) for rerank or moving the reranker to a GPU-quantized instance to keep tails low. Marissa included two rows in the attachment with configuration examples.

I’ll tee up the Terraform snippets and PrivateLink DNS name by EOD Mon; Ben will follow on the cert workflow. Can you confirm which AWS account/Hosted zone you’ll use for the private record?

-Jordan

Attachments: reranker-latency-note-sheet.csv
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Raftlytics onramp: cert rotation, split-DNS & reranker latency tradeoffs

Alex — quick technical note on cert rotation and verification hooks: 

- If you bring your own CA-signed client certs, Redwood will require a PEM bundle (cert + intermediates) for verification. We’ll configure the runtime to only accept connections that present a valid client cert matching the CN/SAN agreed tag (we can lock by SAN to the RAFT service account).
- Rotation: recommend a 30-day rotation window with an overlap period (old cert valid for additional 48 hours) to avoid rollovers. Our onboarding automation can accept a new cert via signed S3 upload or an API call (we’ll provide a signed pre-signed URL).
- Monitoring: we’ll wire a healthcheck that verifies mTLS handshake success rate and surface spikes in handshake failures in the Redwood Console.

Action: can you upload a CA bundle to the secure folder I’ll share in Drive? I’ll generate the pre-signed URL and post it to the HubSpot deal thread.

-ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ryu <alex@raftlytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Raftlytics onramp: cert rotation, split-DNS & reranker latency tradeoffs

Alex/Helen — adding operational considerations from the embeddings team: 

- If you want predictable p95, we can pre-warm reranker instances and reserve a small dedicated pool under Redwood Dedicated for your production namespace (this can be part of your committed capacity). That will reduce variance but increases cost.
- Caching: consider a short TTL prefix cache for popular queries — this reduces token and embedding calls significantly.

Proposed final checklist before handoff call: 
- Confirm AWS account + hosted zone name (Alex)
- Upload CA bundle to shared secure folder (Alex)
- Redwood to provide PrivateLink DNS name and Terraform snippet (Jordan)
- Redwood to create pre-signed upload URL for certs (Ben)
- Decide on reranker capacity model: pooled dedicated vs. burst (Raftlytics + Redwood)

I’ll prepare a 15-minute technical appendix to run during the handoff call focused on p95 mitigation strategies (will share slides).

—Marissa
